chrys

Installation

Node.js


npm install chrys

Python


pip install chrys

Sass


npm install chrys

Usage

Get a list of colours

Omit n to return every available colour: discrete palettes return their largest available size; continuous palettes return the full 256-colour ramp. Pass n to limit the result, or mode to override automatic continuous/discrete selection.

Node.js


import {VEGA_ACCENT, getPaletteColors} from 'chrys';

const colors = getPaletteColors(VEGA_ACCENT);
            

["#7fc97f", "#beaed4", "#fdc086", "#ffff99", "#386cb0", "#f0027f", "#bf5b17", "#666666"]
            

import {VEGA_VIRIDIS, getPaletteColors} from 'chrys';

const colors = getPaletteColors(VEGA_VIRIDIS, 5, 'discrete');
            

["#443a83", "#31688e", "#21918d", "#35b779", "#8fd744"]

Python


from chrys.palettes import VEGA_ACCENT
from chrys.utils import get_palette_colors

hex_colors = get_palette_colors(VEGA_ACCENT)
            

["#7fc97f", "#beaed4", "#fdc086", "#ffff99", "#386cb0", "#f0027f", "#bf5b17", "#666666"]
            

from chrys.palettes import VEGA_VIRIDIS
from chrys.utils import PaletteMode, get_palette_colors

hex_colors = get_palette_colors(VEGA_VIRIDIS, 5, mode=PaletteMode.DISCRETE)
            

["#443a83", "#31688e", "#21918d", "#35b779", "#8fd744"]

Sass


@import 'node_modules/chrys/src/variables';

$palette: map-get(map-get($chrys-palettes, 'vega-accent'), 5);
            

["#7fc97f", "#beaed4", "#fdc086", "#ffff99", "#386cb0"]

Import a single palette

Import only the utility and palette data you need to keep JavaScript bundles small.

Node.js


import toDiscreteColors from 'chrys/utils/to-discrete-colors';
import {BOKEH_VIRIDIS_PALETTE_DATA} from 'chrys/palettes/bokeh/viridis';

const colors = toDiscreteColors(BOKEH_VIRIDIS_PALETTE_DATA, 6);
            

["#440154", "#404387", "#29788e", "#22a784", "#79d151", "#fde724"]

getPaletteColors(name, n, mode) resolves names through the full palette registry and includes all palette data. mode accepts auto (default), continuous, or discrete. Use toDiscreteColors or toContinuousColors with an explicit *_PALETTE_DATA constant when bundle size matters.

Get a list of qualified palette names

Node.js


import {VEGA_PALETTE_NAMES} from 'chrys';

const variables = Object.keys(VEGA_PALETTE_NAMES);
const names = Object.values(VEGA_PALETTE_NAMES);
            

["VEGA_GREENS", "VEGA_YELLOW_GREEN", "VEGA_GOLD_GREEN", ...]
["vega_greens", "vega_yellowgreen", "vega_goldgreen", ...]

Python


from chrys.palettes import VEGA_PALETTE_NAMES

variables = VEGA_PALETTE_NAMES.keys()
names = VEGA_PALETTE_NAMES.values()
            

["VEGA_GREENS", "VEGA_YELLOW_GREEN", "VEGA_GOLD_GREEN", ...]
["vega_greens", "vega_yellowgreen", "vega_goldgreen", ...]

Parse a qualified palette name

Get the vendor and the vendor-specific palette name used internally by the vendor. For example, in Altair and Vega, this is the scheme name.

Node.js


import {VEGA_ACCENT, parsePaletteName} from 'chrys';

parsePaletteName(VEGA_ACCENT);
            

{vendor: "vega", palette: "accent"}

Python


from chrys.palettes import VEGA_CATEGORY_10
from chrys.utils import parse_palette_name

vendor, name = parse_palette_name(VEGA_CATEGORY_10)
            

("vega", "category10")

Colour schemes

Categorical schemes

Categorical colour schemes can be used to encode discrete data values, each representing a distinct category.[1]

Sequential schemes

Sequential colour schemes can be used to encode quantitative values. These colour ramps are designed to encode increasing numeric values. Multi-hue schemes use additional hues for more colour discrimination, which may be useful for visualisations such as heatmaps. However, beware that using multiple hues may cause viewers to inaccurately see the data range as grouped into colour-coded clusters.[1]

Diverging schemes

Diverging colour schemes can be used to encode quantitative values with a meaningful mid-point, such as zero or the average value. Color ramps with different hues diverge with increasing saturation to highlight the values below and above the mid-point.[1]

Cyclical schemes

Cyclical colour schemes may be used to highlight periodic patterns in continuous data. However, these schemes are not well suited to accurately convey value differences.[1]
